assertion: U.S. traffic deaths fell 2.5% to an estimated 16,750 in the first half of 2026, down from 17,175 during the same period in 2025.
reason: NHTSA early estimate (preliminary); 16,750/17,175 = -2.47%. Read via Reuters copy on AOL; NHTSA page returned 403.

assertion: The fatality rate fell to 1.02 per 100 million vehicle miles traveled, the lowest since 2014.
inaccuracy: 1.02 matches NHTSA; 'lowest since 2014' is Reuters' characterization I could not confirm from NHTSA tables.

assertion: The number of deaths fell to the lowest since 2015.
reason: Warehouse FARS annual totals 2014 32,744 vs 2015 35,484; consistent with a first-half low since 2015 (half-year series not in warehouse).
sql: SELECT year, SUM(fatalities) FROM transport.fatal_crashes GROUP BY year

assertion: On pace to be the fifth straight year of declines.
reason: FARS: 2021 43,230 > 2022 42,721 > 2023 41,025 > 2024 39,254, with 2025 reported lower; 2026 would be the fifth. A projection.
sql: SELECT year, SUM(fatalities) FROM transport.fatal_crashes GROUP BY year

assertion: Traffic deaths surged during the pandemic, rising 10.8% in 2021 to 43,230, the highest annual toll since 2005.
sql: SELECT year, SUM(fatalities) FROM transport.fatal_crashes GROUP BY year

assertion: Full-year 2025 deaths fell to the lowest since 2019 and the rate was 1.10, second-lowest yearly figure in US history.
inaccuracy: 2025 not in warehouse; consistent with FARS 2019 36,355 < 2020-2024 all higher. Rate from NHTSA via Reuters only.
sql: SELECT year, SUM(fatalities) FROM transport.fatal_crashes GROUP BY year

assertion: Traffic deaths fell 5% in the first three months of 2026 compared with a year earlier, but declined just 0.2% in the second quarter.
inaccuracy: NHTSA's earlier Q1 release said -4.3%; later revised to about 5% per Reuters. Revision, not error.

assertion: The number killed rose 4% to 1,148 in 2025.
inaccuracy: Not in warehouse; reported by NHTSA via Reuters, primary page 403.

assertion: Experts said emptier roads and a perception that police were less likely to issue tickets contributed to riskier driving.
inaccuracy: Attributed to unnamed experts; consistent with NHTSA/GHSA literature but not tested here.
independent_value: Reuters attribution to experts; widely reported by NHTSA/GHSA

assertion: A NHTSA study released in 2023 estimated that crashes cost society $340 billion, including $30 billion paid by taxpayers.
reason: Matches NHTSA's 2023 economic and societal cost report (2019 data), as relayed by Reuters.
